Hi Alex / Emma — thanks, happy to lead the technical deep-dive. Answers inline to help scope the call:

1) OAuth service accounts (JWT) vs API keys
- For backend server-to-server integrations (GCP -> Redwood), we recommend service accounts with short-lived JWTs (signed by your KMS) when you need per-service identity, granular IAM, and clear rotation policies.
- Pros: short-lived creds, easy revocation via identity provider, better auditability.
- Cons: slightly more setup (service account creation, key management) but we provide SDK helpers.

If you prefer API keys (for simplicity), use fine-grained keys per environment + automated rotation (store keys in KMS/Secret Manager and swap keys using feature flags). Avoid long-lived keys without rotation.

2) SDK support for refresh + rotation
- Our Python/Node SDKs include a TokenProvider helper that can call your identity provider to exchange a signed JWT for a Redwood short-lived token. See attached sdk-setup.zip (examples/refresh_helper.py). We also support an API-key adapter that will rotate keys on a configurable interval and hot-reload without dropping connections.

3) Embeddings & reranker flow (sample)
- Typical pattern:
- Create ephemeral embedding vectors for query + candidate documents (do not persist PII embeddings unless you have an approved retention policy).
- Use a lightweight cosine similarity pass to shortlist candidates, then call our reranker endpoint passing the top-N texts + context for a final scored ordering.
- Example request pattern in SDK: embeddings.generate -> local ANN -> reranker.scoreBatch (attached sample in sdk-setup.zip).

4) Security/SOC2 packet
- Attached security-snapshot.pdf includes a SOC2 summary and our contact for full compliance requests. If you need the full SOC2 report, we can initiate an NDA and a secure transfer via our compliance portal.

Routing note: to route traffic to dedicated capacity or a specific region, set X-Redwood-Route: region=us-west-2;pool=dedicated-fintechco. We can also provide per-tenant routing keys for multi-tenant setups.

Structured output / tool calling: our function-calling support returns a deterministic JSON schema when provided with a tool manifest. Recommend including schema validation in your service to avoid hallucination.

Proposed agenda for deep-dive (30-45m)
- Auth & key rotation patterns (15m)
- SDK walkthrough + token refresh code (10m)
- Embeddings/reranker architecture + sample requests (10m)
- Q&A / next steps (5-10m)

I attached: sdk-setup.zip (code samples), security-snapshot.pdf (SOC2 summary). If you want, I can paste the curl examples into the calendar invite so your engineers can test beforehand. Does 2026-09-03 10:00 AM PT work?

Thanks,

Dev Patel
